Thank you for those details. You mentioned a 2-month history of worsening fatigue with pallor and abnormal blood findings; have you noticed any shortness of breath, dizziness when standing, or changes in your appetite?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with indices, Ferritin, TIBC, and Vitamin B12 levels.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 8.3 g/dL (low); WBC: 81,000 /mm3 (elevated); Platelets: 35,600 /mm3 (low); Ferritin: Not reported; TIBC: Not reported; Vitamin B12: Not reported.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The CBC results show significant abnormalities: severe anemia (Hemoglobin 8.3 g/dL), leukocytosis (WBC 81,000/mm³), and thrombocytopenia (Platelets 35,600/mm³), indicating a bone marrow process rather than simple nutritional deficiency. Given the combination of anemia with high white blood cells and low platelets, are you experiencing any bone pain, fevers, or easy bruising?

REQUEST TEST: Peripheral Blood Smear.
REQUEST IMAGES: Peripheral_Blood_Smear.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Peripheral Blood Smear Findings: Presence of immature cells with large, prominent nucleoli and pink, elongated, needle-shaped cytoplasmic inclusions.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The peripheral blood smear findings of immature cells with large nucleoli and pink, needle-shaped cytoplasmic inclusions (Auer rods) are pathognomonic for acute myeloid leukemia. Given your age and the severe pancytopenia, have you noticed any gum hypertrophy, skin bruising, or visual changes?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)
